title: SSE fallback + typed-output handoff for function-invoke compatibility
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: Clients use our SSE-based streaming API for long-running generations that may include function invocations (tool calls) and structured JSON outputs. In practice we see two recurring failure modes: 1) edge proxies or flaky clients reconnect and reassemble streams incorrectly, breaking function-invocation atomicity; 2) legacy JSONL/EventSource consumers expect newline-delimited JSON and cannot parse our richer structured frames.

Objective: Define and implement a compact SSE fallback/handoff protocol and client compatibility shim that preserves: (a) deterministic function-invocation boundaries, (b) typed/validated structured outputs (schema tokens), and (c) safe reconnect/rewind semantics for both modern and legacy clients. The solution should be low-latency, incremental, and minimally invasive to existing runtime and client SDKs.
technical_design:
Summary: Introduce a minimal wire envelope and handshake tokens layered over SSE. Key concepts: 

- Envelope: Each SSE data chunk will be a length-prefixed, UTF-8 string that begins with a short header: "H:TYPE:SEQID[:CHK]" where TYPE in {TEXT,STRUCT,TOOL,HEARTBEAT,END}. SEQID is a monotonic per-session integer. CHK is an optional 8-char checksum for chunk provenance. Example payload: "H:TOOL:1337:ab12cd34
{\"tool\":\"fetch_db\",\"args\":{...}}".

- Atomic tool invocation marker: Tools are emitted as a single SEQID range with a start marker (TYPE=TOOL, meta=start) and an end marker (TYPE=TOOL, meta=end). The runtime guarantees either full delivery of the range or a clear error/rollback indicator on reconnect.

- Typed structured frames: STRUCT frames contain a schema token in header (e.g., STRUCT:v1/order.v2) and a compact JSON payload. Clients can validate by schema id or ignore if unsupported.

- Reconnect handshake: Clients may present the last-acknowledged SEQID and an optional session HMAC token. Server offers one of: (a) fast-resume by streaming remaining SEQIDs, (b) safe-rewind starting from a stable checkpoint (last completed TOOL end), or (c) full-restart if state cannot be reconciled. The server communicates the decision via a special HEARTBEAT frame with decision codes.

- Backpressure and idempotency: Include a small trailing ack/soft-ack metadata in HEARTBEAT frames that hints how many input tokens were consumed and whether KV cache state was advanced. This allows proxies to coordinate retry semantics without full state sync.

Trade-offs: Adds a ~12-40 byte header per chunk (space overhead vs parsing safety). Using short SEQIDs keeps runtime and proxies efficient. We avoid transferring full session state to reduce memory/attestation complexity.

Security: Session HMACs for reconnects are optional for public endpoints, required for Private. HMAC rotation handled by the existing control plane key API.
implementation_notes: Runtime: Add header encoder/decoder at the output layer and a reconnect decision API (runtime PR #6842). See https://github.com/redwood-inference/inference-runtime/pull/6842
API: SDKs (js/py) will expose two new helpers: StreamEnvelope.parse and StreamEnvelope.handshake. JS PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/1291

Proxy: Edge proxy shim will map legacy newline-json clients to the envelope by translating STRUCT frames into newline-delimited JSON (best-effort) when client sets Accept: application/x-ndjson. Proxy changes tracked in infra repo PR #98

Backward compatibility: If client does not support envelope handshake, server falls back to current JSONL lines but marks TOOL frames with a best-effort wrapper event: event: legacy-tool-hint
 data: {"seq":1337, "status":"partial"}
Metrics: Add counters for reconnect decisions, tool-invoke completion rate, and envelope-parse failures. Dashboards: runtime/streaming/envelope-2026.
testing_plan: Unit tests for header encoder/decoder across edge cases (binary-safe payloads, truncated frames). Integration tests: simulate network flakiness with a local proxy that cuts connections mid-TOOL range and assert server decision codes and client-visible rollback/continue behaviors. Compatibility tests: run legacy ndjson client suite and modern SDK suite against a compatibility proxy. Performance: benchmark 95th percentile extra latency per token at p50/p95 under 1kRPS with envelope enabled; target <1.5ms added p95 overhead on production-like hardware.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): runtime and SDKs behind feature flag for 10% of hosted traffic; enable detailed logs and reconnect metrics. Phase 2: proxy translation enablement in selected regions for customers opting in. Phase 3: full enable for new streaming sessions and documented migration guidance for partners. Provide opt-out header for customers that require legacy behavior (Streaming-Compat: legacy).
acceptance_criteria: Server emits envelope headers for all SSE frames when feature flag is enabled
SDKs correctly parse STRUCT and TOOL ranges and surface typed events to callers via a stable API
Reconnect tests demonstrate server returns fast-resume or safe-rewind consistent with last-ack SEQID in >=99.5% of simulated flake scenarios
Legacy clients behind compatibility proxy see no user-visible regression in >99% of recorded sessions
Performance regression on p95 token latency remains <=1.5ms (envelope on vs off) on bench hardware
